title: Justice Minister Confirms 2028 Election Will Be Held to Re-Elect Erdoğan
detail: Justice Minister Akın Gürlek told AKP lawmakers that 'an election will be held to re-elect our esteemed President,' the first official confirmation that Erdoğan intends to seek re-election via early elections called by parliament. A presidential adviser had floated April 16, 2028 — the anniversary of the 2017 referendum establishing the presidential system — as the target date; under Article 116 of the constitution, parliament (not the president) must call the early vote with 360 of 600 votes, well beyond the AKP-MHP bloc's roughly 326 seats.
confidenceReason: Confirms and builds on an adviser's earlier proposal, but the parliamentary supermajority vote required to enable an early election has not occurred.

media.caption: Justice Minister Akın Gürlek tells AKP lawmakers an election will be held to re-elect Erdoğan

title: Turkey Revokes 44-Year Operating License of Iran's Bank Mellat in Istanbul
detail: Turkey's Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency (BDDK) revoked the operating license of the Istanbul main branch of Iran's Bank Mellat, ending 44 years of operation since 1982, in a decision published in the Official Gazette on September 19 without a public announcement citing US sanctions. The regulator invoked a banking-law clause permitting revocation when continued operation threatens depositor rights or financial-system stability; the move follows expanding US pressure on financial hubs seen as enabling Iranian state trade, and Bank Mellat has long faced US, EU and UK sanctions over alleged links to Iran's nuclear and missile programs.

media.caption: Turkey revokes the Istanbul operating license of Iran's Bank Mellat
